about.title: Sierra Madre Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Sierra Madre residents often travel to nearby Los Angeles County facilities for surgery, imaging, or specialist care, and most visits go fine. But when a provider misses a clear warning sign, mishandles anesthesia, or sends a patient home with the wrong medication, the harm can be serious and lasting. California treats these claims differently than a typical injury case — there are strict notice rules, shortened filing windows, and a requirement that a qualified medical expert review the case before it moves forward. A bad result by itself isn't proof of malpractice; the law asks whether the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care. Our team listens to what happened, reviews your medical records, consults the right experts, and explains whether your situation may support a claim — all without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What Sierra Madre Families Should Know Before Acting

items.title: The Clock Moves Fast Under MICRA
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. We can help pin down which deadline applies to your specific timeline.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Often Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed, California law usually requires sending the provider 90 days' written notice. Missing this step or doing it incorrectly can complicate a case, so early legal guidance matters.

items.title: Expert Review Isn't Optional
items.desc: Almost every California malpractice claim needs a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was violated. Our team works with these experts as part of evaluating whether a claim is viable.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery near Sierra Madre — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. We can review your records to help determine whether the treatment itself was the problem.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim if I live in Sierra Madre?
items.answer: Under MICRA, it's generally one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, and no more than three years from the date it occurred. Because these deadlines are strict and can be affected by the case's specific facts, it's worth getting a timeline reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. Our initial case review is free, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.
